title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page holds only three faint lines in blue pencil. They finish the example begun at the foot of p.55, which ends with 'TSVP'.

Context on p.55: Grothendieck proves that, for a suitable class Σ of 'exact' sequences and a k-linear target category B, evaluation on a canonical complex 𝕃 gives an equivalence (or under weaker hypotheses a fully faithful functor with a retraction σ, σρ ≃ id). The source is the category of k-linear Σ-left-exact functors from a k-linear category 𝒫_· (built from finite/perfect objects); the target is the category B^· of complexes in B. A functor F corresponds to a Σ-resolution C^· = F(𝕃^·) exactly when F is Σ-exact. The example then takes B = Ab_k and λ_· ∈ Ab_{k_·}, and considers the representable functor L_· ↦ Hom(λ_·, L_·), which is claimed to be Σ-left-exact (indeed left exact).

This page: 'la vérification (identification?) de la formule [ou fonct.] : Hom_·(λ_·, L_·) ⥲ Hom(L_·^∨, λ_·^∨) → évidente —'. The claim is that the identification of the representable functor with Hom(L^∨, λ^∨) is obvious. That identification is the natural isomorphism given by transposition (dualization L ↦ L^∨ = Hom_k(L, k)). It is an anti-equivalence on the finite projective / perfect objects in 𝒫, i.e. the reflexivity L ≅ L^∨∨.

Purpose: to recognize the corresponding complex C^· = F(𝕃^·) as the dual complex, so that the example fits the representability statement of p.55. This prepares p.57, which constructs 𝒫 canonically from 𝒜 via the object Ψ^0 representing L ↦ Hom(L, C^0)^∨, i.e. again a duality/transposition argument.

The rest of the page is blank. The thread is simply closed as 'évidente'.
errors: No mathematical content to check beyond a standard identification. The isomorphism Hom(λ,L) ≅ Hom(L^∨, λ^∨) requires reflexivity (finite projective/perfect objects), presumably assumed in context but not stated on the page.

ideas.what: Natural isomorphism Hom(λ, L) ≅ Hom(L^∨, λ^∨) by transposition, for reflexive (finite projective) objects; used to identify a representable Σ-exact functor with a dual complex
ideas.modern_name: Duality anti-equivalence on perfect/finite projective modules (transpose)
ideas.where_published: Standard throughout EGA/SGA (e.g. dualities on perfect complexes, SGA 6)
